papers.title: Structured Feedback Improves Repair in an LLM Agent Loop
papers.claim: Information-equivalent repair feedback that exposes failure location, observed value, and admissible alternatives can improve repair relative to raw diagnostics.

hypothesis: Information-equivalent structured verifier feedback produces fewer invalid follow-up edits and more completions within three attempts than raw output.
null_hypothesis: After equalizing information and token budget, feedback shape does not improve completion, attempts, or invalid-edit rate.
independent_variable: Raw stdout/stderr versus a deterministic information-equivalent feedback adapter.

environment.network_justification: A named model provider will be selected before preregistration.

randomness.justification: Model sampling will be frozen with the provider choice.

metrics.acceptance_rule: No promotion unless repeated wins survive information-equivalence review and discordant pairs are inspected.

evaluator.rubric: Each task completes only when its frozen mechanical verifier passes; manually classify invalid and wrong-location edits.
